solution_pseudocode: Use DP where dp[i][j] is the minimum edits to transform the first i characters of A into the first j of B. Match characters diagonally; otherwise take 1 + min(delete, insert, replace).

title: Solve the Matrix Chain Multiplication problem (minimum multiplication cost)
problem_statement: Given a sequence of matrices, find the most efficient way to multiply these matrices together (minimum scalar multiplications).
constraints_text: 2 \le N \le 100, where matrix dimensions array size is N.
solution_pseudocode: Let dp[i][j] be the minimum scalar multiplications for matrices i..j. Try every split k and update dp[i][j] with left cost + right cost + multiplication cost. Return dp[1][n].

title: Find the maximum sum of non-adjacent elements in an array (House Robber)
problem_statement: You are a robber planning to rob houses along a street. Each house has money, but adjacent houses have security systems connected. Return max money.
solution_pseudocode: Keep prev2 and prev1. For each house x, current = max(prev1, prev2 + x); shift prev2=prev1 and prev1=current. Return prev1.

title: Find the minimum path sum from top-left to bottom-right of a grid
problem_statement: Given an M \times N grid filled with non-negative numbers, find a path from top-left to bottom-right which minimizes the sum of all numbers along its path.
solution_pseudocode: Fill a DP grid where dp[i][j] = grid[i][j] + min(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1]), using proper boundary initialization. Return dp[m-1][n-1].

title: Count unique paths from top-left to bottom-right of a grid with obstacles
problem_statement: An M \times N grid contains obstacles (1). Count unique paths from (0,0) to (M-1, N-1) moving only right or down.
solution_pseudocode: Backtrack from (0,0). Move right or down while inside the grid, append each cell to the current path, and record the path when reaching the bottom-right.

title: Determine whether a set can be split into two subsets of equal sum
problem_statement: Given an integer array nums, return true if you can partition the array into two subsets such that the sum of elements in both subsets is equal.
solution_pseudocode: Compute total sum; if odd return false. Use 0/1 subset-sum DP to determine whether sum/2 can be formed.

title: Find the maximum profit from a single buy/sell of a stock over given daily prices
problem_statement: Given array prices where prices[i] is price on day i, maximize profit by choosing a single day to buy and a future day to sell.
solution_pseudocode: Track the minimum price seen so far and the maximum profit. For each price, update profit with price-minPrice, then update minPrice.

title: Find the maximum profit from unlimited buy/sell transactions on a stock
problem_statement: You may complete as many transactions as you like (i.e., buy one and sell one share of the stock multiple times). Find max profit.
solution_pseudocode: For each day after the first, add max(0, prices[i]-prices[i-1]) to profit.

title: Find the maximum profit from stock trading with at most two transactions
problem_statement: Find the maximum profit you can achieve given stock prices array with at most two transactions.
solution_pseudocode: Track four states: best after first buy, first sell, second buy, second sell. Update them for each price in that order and return second-sell.

title: Find the longest palindromic subsequence in a string using DP
problem_statement: Given a string s, find the length of the longest palindromic subsequence in s.
solution_pseudocode: Use interval DP. For single characters dp[i][i]=1. For increasing lengths, if s[i]==s[j], use inner length + 2; otherwise take max of excluding either end.

title: Solve Word Break using DP (check if a string segments into dictionary words)
problem_statement: Use dynamic programming table to determine if string s can be formed by concatenating words from dictionary wordDict.
solution_pseudocode: Use dp[i] = true when prefix s[0:i] can be segmented. For each i, test every prior split j and set dp[i] if dp[j] is true and s[j:i] is in the dictionary.

title: Find the number of ways to decode a numeric string into letters (Decode Ways)
problem_statement: Given a string s containing digits, return the number of ways to decode it where 'A' -> 1, ..., 'Z' -> 26.
solution_pseudocode: Let dp[i] be ways to decode the first i characters. Add dp[i-1] when the current digit is non-zero; add dp[i-2] when the last two digits form 10..26.

title: Find the largest square of all 1s in a binary matrix (Maximal Square)
problem_statement: Given an M \times N binary matrix filled with 0's and 1's, find the largest square containing only 1's and return its area.
solution_pseudocode: For each cell containing 1, dp[i][j] = 1 + min(top, left, diagonal). Track the largest side and return side squared.

title: Solve the Egg Dropping puzzle (minimum trials to find the critical floor)
problem_statement: You have K eggs and a building with N floors. Find the minimum number of moves required to determine with certainty the highest floor from which an egg can be dropped without breaking.
solution_pseudocode: Use DP over eggs and floors, trying each dropping floor and taking 1 + max(brokenCase, notBrokenCase); optimize with binary search or moves-based DP when desired.

title: Find the minimum number of jumps to reach the end of an array using DP
problem_statement: Compute minimum jumps to reach last index using 1D DP array DP[i] = 1 + \min(DP[j]).
solution_pseudocode: Initialize dp[0]=0 and others infinity. For each index i, update every reachable j in i+1..i+nums[i] with dp[j] = min(dp[j], dp[i]+1). Return dp[n-1].

title: Solve the Rod Cutting problem (maximize revenue from cutting a rod)
problem_statement: Given a rod of length N and an array of prices that includes prices of all pieces of size smaller than N, determine the maximum value obtainable by cutting up the rod and selling the pieces.
solution_pseudocode: Let dp[len] be maximum value for a rod of length len. For every len, try each first cut c and maximize price[c] + dp[len-c].

title: Count the number of Boolean parenthesizations that evaluate to true
problem_statement: Given a boolean expression of operands (T, F) and operators (&, |, ^), count the number of ways to parenthesize the expression so that it evaluates to true.
solution_pseudocode: Use interval DP storing trueWays[i][j] and falseWays[i][j]. For each operator split, combine left/right true/false counts according to &, |, ^. Return trueWays for the full expression.

title: Find the longest common substring (not subsequence) of two strings
problem_statement: Given two strings s1 and s2, find the length of the longest common continuous substring.
solution_pseudocode: Use DP where dp[i][j] is the length of the common suffix ending at s1[i-1], s2[j-1]. If equal, dp = diagonal + 1; otherwise zero. Track the maximum.

title: Solve Activity Selection (maximum non-overlapping activities)
problem_statement: Given N activities with start and finish times, select the maximum number of activities that can be performed by a single person (non-overlapping).
solution_pseudocode: Sort activities by finish time. Select the first one, then repeatedly choose the next activity whose start is at least the last selected finish.

title: Solve the fractional Knapsack problem greedily
problem_statement: Given weights and values of N items and knapsack capacity W, calculate maximum total value where items can be broken into smaller fractions.
solution_pseudocode: Compute value/weight for every item, sort descending by ratio, then take as much as possible from each item until capacity is full.

title: Find the minimum coins for a value greedily, and explain when greedy fails
problem_statement: Given canonical coin denominations \\{1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 500, 2000\\} and target amount V, find minimum coins needed using greedy approach.
solution_pseudocode: Sort coin denominations descending. Take as many of the largest coin as possible, then continue with smaller coins. Greedy is correct for canonical coin systems but can fail for arbitrary denominations.

title: Solve Job Sequencing to maximize profit within deadlines
problem_statement: Given a set of N jobs where each job i has a deadline and profit, find maximum profit earned if only one job can be scheduled at a time unit.
solution_pseudocode: Sort jobs by descending profit. For each job, place it in the latest available slot on or before its deadline; skip it when no slot exists.

title: Find the minimum number of meeting rooms required for a list of intervals
problem_statement: Given an array of meeting time intervals consisting of start and end times [start_i, end_i], find the minimum number of conference rooms required.
solution_pseudocode: Sort start times and end times separately. Use two pointers; when a meeting starts before the earliest ending meeting, increment room count, otherwise decrement it. Track the maximum.

title: Construct a Huffman encoding for a set of characters and frequencies
problem_statement: Given N characters and their frequencies, construct a Huffman tree and print prefix-free binary codes for each character.
solution_pseudocode: Push all characters with frequencies into a min-heap. Repeatedly remove the two least frequent nodes, merge them, and reinsert. Traverse the final tree to assign 0/1 codes.

title: Distribute candies satisfying rating-based constraints with minimum total candies
problem_statement: There are N children standing in a line with ratings. Each child must get at least 1 candy. Children with a higher rating than neighbors get more candies.
solution_pseudocode: Give every child one candy. Scan left-to-right increasing runs and right-to-left decreasing runs; each child gets max(left requirement, right requirement). Sum the candies.

title: Find the minimum number of refueling stops to reach a destination (gas station problem)
problem_statement: A car starts with startFuel gas. Stations are located along the route. Find minimum refueling stops to reach target distance using Max-Heap.
solution_pseudocode: Process stations reachable with the current fuel and push their fuel amounts into a max-heap. When fuel is insufficient to reach the next station, refuel using the largest available amount; count stops.

title: Implement a Min-Heap and a Max-Heap from scratch, with insert and extract operations
problem_statement: Design custom Min-Heap and Max-Heap classes supporting insert(x), extractMin() / extractMax(), and heapify() operations using array storage.
solution_pseudocode: Represent each heap in an array. Insert by appending and bubbling upward while the heap property is violated. Extract-root by swapping with the last item, shrinking the heap, and heapifying downward; reverse the comparison for max-heap.

title: Find the K closest points to the origin from a list of points
problem_statement: Given an array of points (x,y) on 2D plane and integer K, return K closest points to origin (0,0) based on Euclidean distance.
solution_pseudocode: Maintain a max-heap of size k using squared distance x*x+y*y. For each point push it; if heap size exceeds k, remove the farthest point.

title: Merge K sorted linked lists using a min-heap
problem_statement: You are given an array of K linked-lists lists, each linked-list is sorted in ascending order. Merge all the linked-lists into one sorted list.
constraints_text: 0 \le K \le 10^4, total nodes \le 10^4. Time: O(N \log K).
solution_pseudocode: Push the head of each non-empty list into a min-heap keyed by node value. Repeatedly extract the smallest node, append it to the result, and push its next node.

title: Find the running median of a stream of numbers using two heaps
problem_statement: Design a data structure that supports adding numbers from a data stream and finding the current median in O(1) time.
solution_pseudocode: Maintain max-heap left and min-heap right. Insert each value into the appropriate heap and rebalance their sizes so they differ by at most one. The median comes from the top(s).

title: Find the top K frequent elements in an array
problem_statement: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return the k most frequent elements.
constraints_text: 1 \le N \le 10^5, -10^4 \le nums[i] \le 10^4, 1 \le k \le \text{number of unique elements}.
solution_pseudocode: Count frequencies with a hash map. Keep a min-heap of size k keyed by frequency. Push each entry and remove the smallest when the heap grows beyond k.

title: Implement a priority-queue-based task scheduler with cooldown constraints
problem_statement: Given CPU tasks represented by characters and a cooldown integer n, return minimum units of time required to finish all tasks.
solution_pseudocode: Count task frequencies. Use a max-heap for available tasks and a queue for tasks waiting until their cooldown ends. At each time unit schedule the most frequent available task or idle.

title: Connect n ropes with minimum total cost, given their lengths, using a min-heap
problem_statement: Given N ropes of different lengths, connect them into one rope. Cost to connect two ropes is equal to sum of their lengths. Minimize total cost.
solution_pseudocode: Push all rope lengths into a min-heap. Repeatedly pop the two smallest, add their sum to total cost, and push the combined rope back.

title: Check whether a given array represents a valid Min-Heap
problem_statement: Given an array of integers arr, determine if it represents a complete binary tree that satisfies the Min-Heap property (parent \le children).
solution_pseudocode: For every index i with children, verify parent[i] <= each child. If all checks pass, the array is a valid min-heap.

title: Check whether a number is a power of two using bit manipulation
problem_statement: Given an integer n, return true if it is a power of two (n > 0 and (n \& (n-1)) == 0).
solution_pseudocode: A positive power of two has exactly one set bit. Return n > 0 and (n & (n-1)) == 0.

title: Count the number of set bits (1s) in a number's binary representation
problem_statement: Write a function that takes an unsigned integer and returns the number of '1' bits it has (Hamming weight).
solution_pseudocode: Initialize count=0. While n is not zero, add n & 1 to count and shift n right by one. Return count.

title: Swap two numbers without using a temporary variable
problem_statement: Given two variables a and b, swap their values using bitwise XOR operations without extra memory.
solution_pseudocode: Use XOR swapping: a = a XOR b; b = a XOR b; a = a XOR b. Do not use the method when both variables refer to the same storage location.

title: Find the two non-repeating numbers in an array where every other number appears twice
problem_statement: An array contains elements where all numbers appear twice except two numbers which appear once. Find those two unique numbers.
constraints_text: 2 \le N \le 10^5, -10^9 \le arr[i] \le 10^9. Time: O(N), Space: O(1).
solution_pseudocode: XOR all elements to get x = a XOR b. Find any set bit in x to split numbers into two groups, then XOR each group separately to recover a and b.

title: Check, set, clear, and toggle the ith bit of a number
problem_statement: Write functions to check if i^{\text{th}} bit is set, set i^{\text{th}} bit to 1, clear i^{\text{th}} bit to 0, and toggle i^{\text{th}} bit of integer N.
solution_pseudocode: Check with (n AND 1<<i), set with n OR 1<<i, clear with n AND NOT(1<<i), and toggle with n XOR 1<<i.

title: Find the position of the rightmost set bit in a number
problem_statement: Given an integer N, return the 1-based position of the rightmost set bit in its binary representation. If no set bit, return 0.
solution_pseudocode: Compute isolated = n AND (-n). The bit position of isolated is the rightmost set bit.

title: Multiply two numbers without the multiplication operator, using bit shifts
problem_statement: Given two positive integers a and b, calculate a \times b using only bitwise left shift, right shift, and addition.
solution_pseudocode: Use binary multiplication: while multiplier > 0, add the current multiplicand when the low bit is set, double the multiplicand, and shift the multiplier right.

title: Implement a Trie (prefix tree) with insert, search, and startsWith operations
problem_statement: Implement Trie class with insert(word), search(word), and startsWith(prefix) methods.
solution_pseudocode: Each node stores children and an end-of-word flag. Insert follows/creates child nodes per character; search follows children and checks the end flag; prefix search only requires the path to exist.

title: Find all dictionary words that can be formed on a letter board using a Trie + DFS (Word Search II)
problem_statement: Given an M \times N board of characters and a list of strings words, return all words present on the board.
solution_pseudocode: Build a Trie from the dictionary. DFS from each board cell, following Trie edges, marking cells visited and recording words when a terminal Trie node is reached; backtrack after each move.

title: Implement autocomplete suggestions for a given prefix using a Trie
problem_statement: Given a list of dictionary words and a search prefix, return all words in the dictionary that start with the prefix in alphabetical order.
solution_pseudocode: Traverse the Trie along the prefix. If the path exists, DFS from that node to collect complete words, stopping after the required number of suggestions.

title: Find the longest word in a dictionary buildable one character at a time, using a Trie
problem_statement: Given array of strings words, find the longest string in words that can be built one character at a time by other words in words.
solution_pseudocode: Insert all words into a set or Trie. Check words in increasing length; a word is buildable when every prefix obtained by removing the last character exists. Track the longest valid word.

title: Find the maximum XOR of two numbers in an array using a bitwise Trie
problem_statement: Given an integer array nums, return the maximum result of nums[i] \oplus nums[j] where 0 \le i \le j < N.
solution_pseudocode: Insert binary representations into a bitwise Trie. For each number, greedily choose the opposite bit at every position to maximize XOR, and track the best value.

title: Reverse a string
problem_statement: Write a function that reverses a string passed as a character array or string in-place.
solution_pseudocode: Use two pointers at the ends of the character array, swap characters, and move inward until the pointers meet.

title: Number is palindrome
problem_statement: Given an integer x, return true if x is a palindrome integer, and false otherwise.
solution_pseudocode: Store the original number. Rebuild its reverse by repeatedly taking the last digit. Compare the reversed number with the original.

title: Binary to decimal
problem_statement: Convert a binary string or binary representation into its equivalent base-10 integer.
solution_pseudocode: Initialize value=0. For each binary digit d, update value = value*2 + d. Return value.

title: Count vowels in string
problem_statement: Given a string s, count the total number of vowels (a, e, i, o, u, case-insensitive) present in it.
solution_pseudocode: Initialize count=0. Scan characters and increment count when the lowercased character is one of a, e, i, o, u.

title: Check prime number
problem_statement: Given a number N, determine whether it is a prime number.
solution_pseudocode: Start from any vertex, push its outgoing edges into a min-heap, and repeatedly take the cheapest edge leading to an unvisited vertex; add the edge and push the new vertex edges.

title: Check Armstrong number
problem_statement: An Armstrong number of K digits is a number equal to sum of K^{\text{th}} power of its digits. Check if given N is Armstrong.
solution_pseudocode: Count the digits. Raise each digit to that digit-count, sum the powers, and compare the sum with the original number.

title: GCD of two numbers
problem_statement: Compute Greatest Common Divisor of two integers a and b using Euclidean Algorithm.
solution_pseudocode: Use Euclid: while b is not zero, set (a,b) = (b, a mod b). Return a.

title: Find LCM
problem_statement: Find Least Common Multiple of two integers a and b using formula \text{LCM}(a,b) = (a \times b) / \text{GCD}(a,b).
solution_pseudocode: Compute g = gcd(a,b). Return abs(a/g*b).

title: Count occurrence of elements
problem_statement: Given an array and a target element X, count how many times X appears in the array.
solution_pseudocode: Use a frequency map. For each element increment its count, then return the map or requested frequencies.

title: String to title case
problem_statement: Convert input string s to Title Case where the first letter of each word is capitalized and rest are lowercase.
solution_pseudocode: Split the string into words. For each word, uppercase the first character and lowercase the remaining characters, then join the words.

title: Missing and repeating number
problem_statement: Given unsorted array of size N containing elements from 1 to N. One number from 1..N is missing and one appears twice. Find both.
solution_pseudocode: Use a frequency array or marking method. The value with count 2 is repeating; the value with count 0 is missing.

title: Number of digits in an integer
problem_statement: Given an integer N, count the total number of digits present in N.
constraints_text: -2^{31} \le N \le 2^{31}-1. Time Complexity: O(1) using \lfloor \log\_{10} N \rfloor + 1.
solution_pseudocode: Handle zero as one digit. Otherwise repeatedly divide the absolute number by 10 and count iterations.

title: Armstrong numbers in range
problem_statement: Given two integers low and high, print all Armstrong numbers in the range [low, high].
solution_pseudocode: For each number in the range, apply the Armstrong-number test and output numbers whose digit-power sum equals the number.

title: Array elements sum
problem_statement: Given an array of integers, compute total sum of all elements.
solution_pseudocode: Initialize total=0 and add every array element to total. Return total.

title: Factorial through loop
problem_statement: Compute factorial of N using an iterative loop.
solution_pseudocode: Initialize result=1. Multiply result by every integer from 2 through n. Return result.

title: Two numbers without temp swapping
problem_statement: Swap values of a and b using arithmetic operators (a = a+b; b = a-b; a = a-b).
solution_pseudocode: Swap the two values without a temporary variable using XOR: a=a XOR b; b=a XOR b; a=a XOR b.

title: Linear search
problem_statement: Search for element X in array of size N. Return first index or -1.
solution_pseudocode: Scan from left to right. Return the index of the first element equal to target; return -1 if target is absent.

title: Add two matrices
problem_statement: Given two M \times N matrices A and B, compute matrix C = A + B.
solution_pseudocode: Create a result matrix of the same dimensions. For each cell, result[i][j] = A[i][j] + B[i][j].

title: Print prime numbers within a range
problem_statement: Given range [L, R], print all prime numbers in the range using Sieve of Eratosthenes.
solution_pseudocode: Start from any vertex, push its outgoing edges into a min-heap, and repeatedly take the cheapest edge leading to an unvisited vertex; add the edge and push the new vertex edges.

title: Print pattern of stars
problem_statement: Print standard pyramid star pattern for N rows.
solution_pseudocode: Use nested loops. The outer loop controls the row and the inner loop prints the required number of stars/spaces for that row according to the pattern.

title: Words in sentence count
problem_statement: Count the number of words in a given string sentence.
solution_pseudocode: Trim the sentence, split on whitespace, and count non-empty tokens.

title: Leap year check
problem_statement: Given year Y, determine if it is a leap year (divisible by 4 and not 100, unless divisible by 400).
solution_pseudocode: A year is leap if divisible by 400, or divisible by 4 but not by 100. Return the corresponding boolean.

title: Duplicates in array remove
problem_statement: Remove duplicate elements from an unsorted array while maintaining unique elements.
solution_pseudocode: Use a set to track seen values. Add each unseen value to the result and skip values already present.

title: Remove white spaces from string
problem_statement: Remove all spaces from a given string in-place.
solution_pseudocode: Scan all characters and append only characters that are not whitespace to the result.

title: Sum of digits of a number
problem_statement: Calculate the sum of all digits of a given integer N.
solution_pseudocode: Initialize sum=0. Repeatedly add n mod 10 and divide n by 10 until n becomes zero.

title: Find median of array
problem_statement: Find the median element of an array after sorting.
solution_pseudocode: Sort the array. If length is odd return the middle value; otherwise return the average of the two middle values.

title: Count set bits in integer
problem_statement: Count total 1s in binary representation of N.
solution_pseudocode: Initialize count=0. While n is not zero, set n = n AND (n-1) and increment count. Return count.

title: Transpose of matrix
problem_statement: Given M \times N matrix A, return its transpose matrix A^T of size N \times M.
solution_pseudocode: Create a transposed matrix T where T[j][i] = A[i][j], or swap A[i][j] with A[j][i] above the diagonal for an in-place square matrix.

title: Calculate power with bitwise
problem_statement: Compute a^b using bitwise right shift to check odd/even powers in O(\log b) time.
solution_pseudocode: Use exponentiation by squaring: while exponent > 0, multiply result when the low bit is set, square the base, then shift exponent right.

title: Merge two strings alternatively
problem_statement: Given two strings s1 and s2, merge them by adding letters in alternating order.
solution_pseudocode: Use two indices and append one character from each string alternately until one string ends, then append the remainder.

title: Find duplicate elements
problem_statement: Find all elements that appear more than once in an array.
solution_pseudocode: Use a set to track seen values. Add each unseen value to the result and skip values already present.

title: Diagonal sum of matrix
problem_statement: Compute the sum of primary and secondary diagonals of an N \times N square matrix.
solution_pseudocode: Sum matrix[i][i] for the main diagonal and matrix[i][n-1-i] for the secondary diagonal. Avoid double-counting the center if n is odd.

title: Subset sum problem
problem_statement: Given a set of non-negative integers and a value sum, determine if there is a subset with sum equal to sum.
solution_pseudocode: Use boolean DP where dp[s] indicates whether sum s is achievable. For each number, update sums from target down to number. Return dp[target].

title: Print boundary of binary tree
problem_statement: Return boundary nodes of a binary tree anti-clockwise starting from root.
solution_pseudocode: Add root, then traverse the left boundary excluding leaves, collect all leaves left-to-right, then traverse the right boundary excluding leaves bottom-to-top.

title: Reverse stack recursively
problem_statement: Reverse a stack using recursion without extra helper stack structures.
solution_pseudocode: Recursively pop the top until the stack is empty. Then insert each popped element at the bottom using another recursive function.

title: Queue using linked list
problem_statement: Implement FIFO Queue using singly linked list nodes with enqueue and dequeue.
solution_pseudocode: Maintain front and rear node pointers. Enqueue by attaching a new node at rear; dequeue by removing front and updating front/rear when the queue becomes empty.

title: Binary tree to DLL
problem_statement: Convert a binary tree to a Doubly Linked List in-place following inorder traversal sequence.
solution_pseudocode: Perform inorder traversal. Link the current node with the previously visited node using left=prev and prev.right=current; update prev each time.

title: Heap sort
problem_statement: Implement Heap Sort algorithm using max heap building and repeated extraction.
solution_pseudocode: Build a max-heap. Repeatedly swap the root with the last unsorted element, reduce heap size, and heapify the root. The array becomes sorted.

title: Celebrity problem using stack
problem_statement: A celebrity is known to everyone but knows no one. Find celebrity in N people given matrix M[i][j] in O(N) time.
solution_pseudocode: Push all people onto a stack. Pop two at a time and discard anyone who cannot be the celebrity based on knows relation. Verify the final candidate knows nobody and everyone knows the candidate.

title: Count set bits using Brian Kernighan's algo
problem_statement: Count set bits in N by repeatedly clearing rightmost set bit (N = N \& (N-1)).
solution_pseudocode: Initialize count=0. While n != 0, set n = n AND (n-1) and increment count. The number of iterations equals the number of set bits.

title: Maximum sum path in matrix
problem_statement: Find maximum path sum starting from any cell in top row to any cell in bottom row, moving down, down-left, down-right.
solution_pseudocode: Use DP from the top row. For each cell, add its value to the maximum of allowed predecessor cells (up/diagonals or according to the problem definition). Track the maximum in the last row.

title: Snake and ladder game simulation
problem_statement: Given board configuration with snakes and ladders, find minimum dice throws to reach destination square 100 using BFS.
constraints_text: Board size 100 cells, up to 30 snakes/ladders.
solution_pseudocode: Model board cells as graph edges from each position to up to six next dice positions, applying snakes/ladders. BFS from start gives the minimum number of dice throws.

title: Count number of BSTs
problem_statement: Given N nodes, count total unique BSTs that can be formed using N^{\text{th}} Catalan number C_N.
solution_pseudocode: Let dp[n] be the number of unique BSTs with n nodes. dp[0]=dp[1]=1. For each n, sum dp[left]*dp[right] over every possible root.

title: Inorder successor in BST
problem_statement: Find the in-order successor of a given node P in a Binary Search Tree.
constraints_text: Number of nodes in [1, 10^4]. Time: O(H).
solution_pseudocode: If node has a right subtree, return its leftmost node. Otherwise walk from the root, moving left when current value is greater than target and remembering that node as successor.

title: Count distinct subsequences
problem_statement: Given a string S, count number of distinct non-empty subsequences modulo 10^9+7.
solution_pseudocode: Use DP over prefixes. For each character c, newCount = 2*dp + 1 minus the number of subsequences previously ending with c. Track last contribution for each character modulo the required modulus.

title: Word ladder
problem_statement: Given two words beginWord and endWord, and a dictionary wordList, return shortest transformation sequence length changing 1 letter at a time.
solution_pseudocode: Use BFS from beginWord. Generate all one-letter mutations that exist in the dictionary, remove visited words, and continue level by level until endWord is found.

title: Evaluation of expression tree
problem_statement: Given a binary expression tree where leaves are values and internal nodes are operators, evaluate total expression value.
solution_pseudocode: Postorder recursively evaluate children. If the node is a value return it; otherwise apply the operator to the evaluated left and right results.

title: Bit manipulation problems
problem_statement: Practice utility functions for single number detection, bit flips required to convert number A to B, and swap nibbles.
solution_pseudocode: Single number: XOR all values. Bit flips A to B: count set bits in A XOR B. Swap nibbles: extract low/high 4-bit groups and exchange their positions.

title: Number of smaller elements to right
problem_statement: Given array nums, return an array counts where counts[i] is the number of smaller elements to the right of nums[i] (using Merge Sort or Segment Tree).
solution_pseudocode: Use merge sort on indexed values. During merge, when taking a right-half value before a left-half value, add the number of remaining smaller right elements to the left index count.

title: Burst balloons problem
problem_statement: Given N balloons with coins, burst all balloons to maximize total coins collected using interval DP.
solution_pseudocode: Add virtual balloons with value 1 at both ends. Use interval DP: choose the last balloon to burst inside each interval and maximize leftDP + value*neighbor values + rightDP.

title: Max points from cards
problem_statement: There are N cards in a row. In one step, take 1 card from beginning or end. Maximize score after taking exactly K cards.
solution_pseudocode: Take x cards from the left and k-x from the right for every x from 0..k. Track the maximum combined sum, or equivalently minimize the sum of the middle n-k cards.

title: Find centroid of a tree
problem_statement: Find a node in a tree such that removing it leaves no connected component with size greater than N/2.
solution_pseudocode: Run DFS to compute subtree sizes. A node is a centroid when every remaining component after removing it has size <= n/2. Return such a node.

title: Convert BST to greater sum tree
problem_statement: Transform a BST such that every key is changed to original key plus sum of all keys greater than original key in BST.
solution_pseudocode: Traverse the BST in reverse inorder (right, root, left) while maintaining a running sum of greater values. Replace each node value with node.value + runningSum before updating the running sum.

title: Longest valid parentheses
problem_statement: Given a string containing just '(' and ')', find the length of the longest valid (well-formed) parentheses substring.
solution_pseudocode: Use a stack of indices initialized with -1. Push the index of each opening parenthesis. For a closing parenthesis, pop; if the stack becomes empty push the current index, otherwise update maximum length as i - stack.top.
